_comment: CXR dataset (CheXpert 'test' split) with NLP-derived classification labels, plus a subset (499/668 images) of per-pathology ground-truth segmentation masks (COCO RLE, from CheXlocalize's gt_segmentations_test.json) used to evaluate saliency-method localization. Masks are unioned across pathologies into a single combined abnormality mask per image, since the RadHarmony pipeline supports one mask per image (see harmonizer notes). Raw radiologist polygon annotations (gt_annotations_test.json), human-benchmark annotations/salient points (hb_*), and Grad-CAM outputs (gradcam_*) exist in the source data but are out of scope for this integration.

primary_csv._comment: The main metadata CSV that lists every image row.

patient_id._comment: No Patient ID column exists in this CSV. Derived from the Path column.
patient_id.derivation: extract 'patient<digits>' from the Path column, e.g. 'test/patient64741/study1/view1_frontal.jpg' -> 'patient64741'

study_id._comment: No study-id column exists. Derived from Path; combined with patient_id for uniqueness (500 unique patients/studies, 668 rows -- studies can have multiple views).
study_id.derivation: extract 'study<digits>' from Path and join with patient_id, e.g. 'patient64741_study1'

image_path._comment: Path column already relative to base_image_dir once the 'test/' prefix is stripped.

labels._comment: Label columns and how to handle uncertain values. Labels live in the primary CSV itself (not a separate file). All values in this test split are strictly 0.0/1.0 -- no -1 uncertainty labels, no NaNs.

separate_csv._comment: Labels are in the primary CSV; no separate label file.

uncertain_handling._comment: No NaN/-1 values present in this split; settings below are defensive defaults and are not expected to trigger.

view_position._comment: Not a CSV column. Derived from the image filename, which encodes 'viewN_frontal' or 'viewN_lateral'.
view_position.source: derived from filename: 'frontal' or 'lateral' substring in the Path basename

masks._comment: Segmentation mask support. Source is gt_segmentations_test.json, keyed by '<study_id>_<view_basename>' -> {pathology: {size:[H,W], counts: COCO-RLE}}, covering 499/668 images. One COCO-RLE mask PER PATHOLOGY per image (up to 10; pathology names in the JSON -- e.g. 'Airspace Opacity', CheXpert's older name for 'Lung Opacity' -- are irrelevant since every mask for an image is unioned regardless of name). RadHarmony's pipeline supports only a single combined mask per image, so all per-pathology masks for an image are unioned (bitwise OR) into one binary 'any abnormal region' mask, following the same union pattern used for multi-row RLE masks in SIIM-ACR. Requires pycocotools for COCO RLE decoding (new dependency, added to pyproject.toml). Images without any entry in the JSON get an all-zero mask when output_mask=True (same convention as SIIM-ACR's no-finding rows).

bboxes._comment: No bounding-box data exists anywhere in the source dataset (checked CSV and CheXlocalize/ directory). Not supported.

reports._comment: No radiology report data found in the source dataset. Not supported.

extra_init_params._comment: mask_json_path: path to gt_segmentations_test.json, required when output_mask=True.

custom_preprocessing: Segmentation masks require decoding COCO RLE via pycocotools and unioning per-pathology masks into one binary mask per image; see 'masks' section.
